diagnosis: Progress has stalled at only $9.6\times10^{-6}$ below the record because the incumbent is not a converged, jammed local optimum: it has essentially one pair exactly at the maximum, only four contacted points within $10^{-9}$, and 178 rattlers. A rigid optimum on $(S^8)^{182}$ has $182\cdot 8-36=1420$ degrees of freedom after removing rotations, so it should require on the order of a thousand active pairs and typically $8$--$16$ contacts per point, not $0.04$. The smooth slack curve, with roughly 1100 pairs trailing within $10^{-6}$ but almost none tied, shows an unequalized near-contact bulk and remaining descent directions that the solvers are abandoning through tiny trust regions, single-pair moves, premature termination, and timeouts. The missing structural property is therefore a balanced, rigid contact graph in which load is spread over most points, rather than one isolated bottleneck pair.
